codebase.title: Mink differential inverse kinematics
codebase.fingerprint_algorithm: SHA-256 over typed sorted regular-file paths+bytes and symlink paths+safe targets

agent_authored.description: Mink is a MuJoCo-based differential inverse-kinematics library. It assembles weighted task objectives and kinematic constraints into a quadratic program, solves for a tangent displacement, and integrates the resulting velocity on the robot configuration manifold. This contribution proposes one core module with Panda SE(3) workloads.

shared_components.title: Shared infrastructure
shared_components.purpose: SE(3) and SO(3) representations, exponential/logarithmic maps, adjoints and Jacobians; optional C hot-path implementations with Python fallbacks; joint-width constants, exceptions, model/frame utilities, API exports and package build configuration.

modules.title: Constrained differential inverse kinematics with Panda SE(3) workloads
modules.expensive_path: Repeated frame residual/Jacobian computation, weighted or dense QP objective construction, inequality/equality assembly, backend solution and kinematic update. Native C hot paths already exist upstream. This report describes the path but makes no performance claim.
modules.rationale: A single manageable source-based module retains the generic solver APIs and their configuration/task/limit contracts rather than defining scope only by the Panda example.
excluded: Additional standalone modules for specialized task families; their source and official examples remain included.
hazards: The Panda model has nine scalar coordinates: seven arm joints and two finger sliders. General models can have nq different from nv.
Ball-joint position limits are first-order linearizations; the upstream documentation recommends a velocity limit to control second-order overshoot.
Pose and posture are soft objectives; successful QP solution or a zero-exit documentation script does not establish target convergence.
The public C-enabled wheel was exercised, but no C compiler was available for a local source build of that extension.
Model-backed tests outside the executed subset and optional viewer examples remain unexecuted.
modules.purpose: Construct and solve constrained differential IK, regulating frame pose and posture while updating robot kinematics and enforcing supported configuration and velocity limits. The boundary follows the reusable solver and task/limit APIs; Panda is the principal example robot, not the definition of the module.
primary_inputs: A MuJoCo model, data and configuration q with nq positions and nv tangent coordinates; those dimensions can differ for free and ball joints.
Frame identifiers and target SE(3) poses, posture targets, task weights, feedback gains and damping.
A positive integration timestep, selected QP backend, optional equality tasks, configuration limits and joint velocity limits.
primary_outputs: build_ik returns a qpsolvers.Problem containing H, c, G, h, A and b, with absent constraint blocks represented as None.
solve_ik returns an nv-dimensional tangent velocity, obtained by dividing the solved displacement by dt, or raises a documented solver/configuration error.
Configuration integration updates joint positions and derived kinematics; pose, Jacobian, residual and constraint APIs expose intermediate mathematical quantities.
algorithm_stages: Refresh MuJoCo kinematics for the current configuration and obtain frame transforms and Jacobians.
Compute frame residuals in SE(3) and posture residuals on configuration space, with their tangent Jacobians.
Apply task weights and gains; stack weighted Jacobians for the quadratic objective, add Levenberg-Marquardt terms and support dense objective contributions.
Assemble configuration and velocity inequalities on the displacement and optional task equalities.
Solve the QP through qpsolvers, check the solver result, convert displacement to velocity, then integrate with MuJoCo's configuration-manifold operation.
unique_responsibilities: Own the solver assembly and orchestration, including dense-objective fallback and equality hooks even when the workload uses only pose/posture objectives.
Own configuration state, frame access, integration, frame and posture objectives, and the abstract task/limit interfaces.
Own hinge/slide position bounds, the linearized limited-ball-joint bound, and supported named-joint velocity bounds. Generic joint indexing is part of the core.
not_responsible_for: MuJoCo's engine, qpsolvers and backend solver internals.

Independent task families for contact/dynamics, collision avoidance, whole-body control, retargeting, teleoperation or training. Their official tests still need relevance accounting wherever they exercise owned or shared APIs.
A new accelerator implementation in this source contribution.
modules.differences: Only one module is proposed. It groups robot state, objective construction, constraints, QP solve and integration because they form the reusable differential-IK pipeline. Lie mathematics and common build/utilities are shared infrastructure. Specialized objectives and limits remain vendored without being claimed as additional modules.

mink-constrained-differential-ik.count_scope: The 13 listed primary framework files, covering the owned core and direct shared Lie/configuration support. Three example paths are contextual sources and do not inflate framework counts. This is not an exhaustive association of all specialist tests with the module.
covers: Configuration indexing, frame transforms, Jacobians, integration and limit error handling.
Frame/posture residuals and Jacobians, task costs, solver objective assembly, solver errors and hard constraint hooks.
Joint configuration and velocity bounds, including non-Panda scalar/ball/free-joint behavior in generic fixtures.
Shared Lie group axioms, operations, numerical Jacobian comparisons and model utilities.
Documentation examples run as subprocesses with exit-code assertions; the Panda example supplies a standard frame/posture IK loop.
known_gaps: Primary-file association is incomplete for specialized objectives/limits that also exercise shared or owned solver paths; those tests remain in the source tree for subsequent examination.

The unchanged Panda convergence function was probed headlessly at a phase-zero circular offset; it did not meet its own termination criterion in one original 20-step call. The original full interactive example was not run.

Documentation subprocess success asserts execution, not scientific accuracy or convergence. GUI/rendering, continuous examples, every solver backend and cross-platform behavior are not certified by these runs.

The full official suite passed as supplied in separate native processes. This does not establish every advertised scientific property: one G1 bound test mixes qpos/tangent indices, and the Talos finite-difference setup does not constrain random samples to legal joint positions.
